2027-07-26.title: Saints Joachim and Anne, Parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary
readings: Alas, this people has sinned a great sin; they have made for themselves gods of gold
Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed ... like yeast
2027-07-26.alt: Memorial. The weekday readings of Week 17 (Year I) are given; the proper readings of the memorial (Sirach 44:1, 10–15; Psalm 132:11, 13–14, 17–18; Matthew 13:16–17) may be used instead. The names Joachim and Anne come from an early Christian writing, the Protoevangelium of James (second century), not from the Gospels. Yesterday, the fourth Sunday of July, was the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly. Psalm verses are the same in NRSV and the Lectionary. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-07-26.verse: Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on generation after generation. The assembly declares their wisdom, and the congregation proclaims their praise.
theo: Moses comes down from Sinai carrying “the two tablets of the covenant,” written on both sides, “the work of God.” Below him is the noise of a party. Joshua thinks it is the sound of war; Moses knows better: “it is the sound of revelers that I hear.” When he sees the calf and the dancing his anger burns, and he shatters the tablets at the foot of the mountain, a picture of a covenant broken. He burns the calf, grinds it to powder and makes the people drink it, to show that the idol is nothing. Then he faces Aaron, who gives one of the most comic and most tragic excuses in the Bible: “I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!” Scripture knows our habit of blaming everything but ourselves. The next day Moses does what the great intercessors do. He tells the people the truth, “You have sinned a great sin,” and then he goes back up the mountain: “perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.” His prayer breaks off in the middle of a sentence: “if you will only forgive their sin” and then, “if not, blot me out of the book that you have written.” He puts his own name on the line for a people who have just betrayed God. The Psalm remembers it: “had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath from destroying them.” The Church sees in Moses a shadow of Christ, who “always lives to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 7:25).

In the Gospel Jesus tells two short parables, the mustard seed and the yeast. The kingdom of heaven does not arrive with trumpets; it begins small, hidden, and works from within. The seed is “the smallest of all the seeds,” yet it becomes a tree where birds nest; the yeast is hidden in “three measures of flour,” enough for a whole village's bread, “until all of it was leavened.” St Matthew adds that Jesus speaks in parables to fulfil the word of the Psalm: “I will proclaim what has been hidden from the foundation of the world” (Psalm 78:2). Beside these parables the Church today places the memory of two hidden people, Joachim and Anne. The Gospels never name them. Their names come from the Protoevangelium of James, a second-century writing that the Church does not count as Scripture, but whose names the faithful have honoured in East and West for many centuries. What the Church knows with certainty is simple: Mary had parents. They received her as God's gift, taught her the psalms and the promises of Israel, and handed on a faith in which she could answer the angel: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” The Church teaches that Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception, yet she was born into a human family, nursed, and taught like any child. A mustard seed of faith passed from grandparents to a girl in Nazareth, and from her the Lord of all took flesh. In Kerala the name of Anne is in every parish, in Annamma and Anna and Ann, and the old stories of Joachim and Anne praying for a child echo the stories of Sarah and Hannah, whose prayer we hear in the Book of Samuel: “if only you will look on the misery of your servant, and remember me” (1 Samuel 1:11).
outline: Ask: who first taught you to pray, and what did they hand on to you without knowing it?
He puts his own name on the line for a people who betrayed God; Christ always lives to intercede.
Point 2 · The mustard seed and the yeast
The kingdom begins small and hidden, and grows from within.
Two hidden people, a faith handed on, and the girl who said: Here am I.
“A faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice.”
live: Choose one person who has gone far from God, and pray for them by name each day this week, as Moses prayed for his people.
Tell a child or grandchild one story of how God has been faithful to your family, or ask a grandparent to tell it to you, and write it down.
saints: According to the Protoevangelium of James, Joachim and Anne were an elderly, childless couple who prayed for a child, and Mary was born to them. The Church honours them as the parents of the Mother of God and, therefore, as the grandparents of Jesus according to the flesh. Anne was honoured in the East from early centuries, and her feast spread to the West in the Middle Ages; Joachim, who had a separate day in the older Roman calendar, was joined to her on 26 July in 1969.
2027-07-26.prayer: O God of our fathers, who gave Saints Joachim and Anne the grace of bringing forth the Mother of your incarnate Son, grant, through the prayers of both, that we may attain the salvation you have promised to your people. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord God, you hide your kingdom in small seeds and quiet lives. Bless our grandparents and parents, who plant the faith in the heart of a child. Make us faithful to what they handed on, and, like Moses, ready to stand in the breach for those who have strayed. Amen.
altar: In every Mass the Church does what Moses did on the mountain: she stands before God for a sinful people, but not with her own merits. She offers the one sacrifice of Christ, “who always lives to make intercession for them.” And in the Eucharistic Prayer we ask to share the company of Mary, the apostles and “all the Saints”: among them, in the hidden ranks of the saints, are the grandparents and parents who taught us to pray and who now pray for us.

quick: Moses finds the people dancing around a golden calf, breaks the tablets, and then goes back up the mountain to plead for them.
Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed and to yeast: small beginnings that grow from within.
Sts Joachim and Anne, the parents of Mary, are remembered as the hidden people who handed on the faith.
2027-07-26.action: Ask a grandparent or an elderly relative to tell you one story of faith from your family.
2027-07-26.question: Whom am I praying for by name, as Moses prayed, and whom did God use to plant the faith in me?
kidsaint: An old book tells us that Joachim and Anne were Mary's parents. They were not young, and they had no children, and they prayed and prayed. Then God gave them a little daughter, Mary, and they taught her to pray the psalms. So Joachim and Anne were the grandparents of Jesus! We do not know many details, and some of the stories are only stories. But we know that grandparents are very special. Many children in Kerala are named Anna or Annamma after St Anne. Lesson: grandparents who pray plant seeds of faith that grow into trees.

family.explain: A mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice. But planted in the ground it grows into a big plant where birds make their nests. Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like that: it begins small and grows. Joachim and Anne were Mary's parents; they loved her and taught her to pray. Their small love grew into something huge, because Mary became the mother of Jesus. Our small prayers and kind acts can grow too.
family.intention: We thank God for our grandparents and for those who taught us to pray, and we pray for those who are far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “What did your grandparents teach you? Who taught them to pray? Shall we ask them to tell us?”

illus: In a Kerala house the evening prayer was always led by the grandmother. She sat on the veranda mat with a rosary, and the grandchildren, tired and sleepy, sat around her and answered the Hail Marys. The grandson grew up, left the village and became a priest. At her funeral he said: I never once heard her give a sermon, but I learned from her what prayer is. My first prayer was in her lap. The seed was so small that none of us noticed it being sown. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you hid the beginnings of our salvation in a quiet family. Teach us to hand on the faith and to pray for those who have strayed. Amen.
share: I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin (Exodus 32:30). For whom would I be ready to stand in the breach?
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed (Matthew 13:31). What small beginning in my family or parish do I think too little to matter?
Who were the Joachim and Anne in my own life, the ones who first taught me to pray, and how can I thank God for them today?
pm.resp: Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may always intercede for the world as Moses did, and hand on the faith to the next generation.
For grandparents and parents, that they may be signs of God's patience and teachers of prayer.
For children and young people who have never heard a prayer at home, and for those who have turned away from the faith.
For couples who long for a child, that, like Joachim and Anne, they may wait and pray in hope.
For our group, that we may be small seeds and hidden yeast for the kingdom.
pm.close: God of our fathers, you gave the Blessed Virgin Mary a father and a mother who taught her your promises. Give us a faith that we can hand on. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the people of Israel have made a golden calf, and Moses has to come down the mountain with the tablets in his hands. He sees the dancing and breaks the tablets. And Aaron, the priest, says: I threw the gold in the fire, and out came this calf! (Exodus 32:24). How like us. We make a mess and then say it just happened.

But look at what Moses does next. He does not wash his hands of them. He goes back up the mountain and prays: forgive them, but if not, blot me out of the book that you have written (Exodus 32:32). That is a leader who stands in the breach. The Psalm says it: had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath (Psalm 106:23). Every one of us has someone who stood in the breach for us: a mother who prayed, a grandfather who fasted, a grandmother who held the rosary.

In the Gospel Jesus says that the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, the smallest of all seeds, and like yeast hidden in flour. God works small and hidden. And today the Church remembers two hidden people. We do not find Joachim and Anne in the Gospels. Their names come from an old book. But we know something certain: Mary had parents, and they taught her to pray and to trust the promises of God. How else could a girl in Nazareth say: Here am I, the servant of the Lord? (Luke 1:38). Faith is always handed on, as St Paul tells Timothy: a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you (2 Timothy 1:5).

Yesterday we kept the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly, and today we honour the grandparents of Jesus. So let us ask: who planted the seed of faith in me? And whose seed am I planting? Let us thank God for them, pray for them, and, like Moses, stand in the breach for those who have strayed. Amen.
kids: Children, a mustard seed is tiny, but when it is planted it grows into a big tree where birds can make their nests. Jesus says God's kingdom is like that. Today we remember Mary's mother and father, Joachim and Anne. They loved little Mary and taught her to pray, and she grew up to be the Mother of Jesus. So Joachim and Anne were Jesus' grandparents! Thank God for your own grandparents today, and ask them to tell you a story about when they were small.

intro: Theme: “A faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice.”
Moses in the breach, the mustard seed, and the hidden grandparents of Jesus: faith is always handed on.

sub: The calf, the broken tablets, Aaron's excuse.
Blot me out of the book.
q: Had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath from destroying them.
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Name one person far from God, and pray for them every day this week, asking to stand in the breach for them.

sub: The smallest of all the seeds.
Yeast hidden in three measures of flour.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.

He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field; it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.”
points.apply: Do one small good thing today that no one will notice, and trust God to make it grow.

q: We will not hide them from their children; we will tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the Lord, and his might, and the wonders that he has done.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Tell one young person this week how you came to believe, and thank the one who first taught you to pray.

concl: Moses shows the heart of an intercessor, who puts his own name on the line for a people who failed.
The kingdom grows from small, hidden beginnings, like the faith that Joachim and Anne handed on to Mary and she to the world.
2027-07-26.resolve: Pray each day for someone far from God, and tell a younger person one story of faith from your family.
